% Pattern: head/italic/article. Seen in the gold pilot (set E): a proof head
% written by hand that names its statement with \ref, in an italic or bold
% group (rule 1). The \ref in the head attaches the proof; it is not a use.
% want theorem-1 statement/theorem 1 status=here labels=main
% want lemma-1 statement/lemma 2 status=here labels=aux
% want head-1 proof - proves=theorem-1
% want head-2 proof - proves=lemma-1
\documentclass{article}
\usepackage{amsthm}
\newtheorem{theorem}{Theorem}
\newtheorem{lemma}[theorem]{Lemma}
\begin{document}
\begin{theorem}\label{main}
The main result.
\end{theorem}
\begin{lemma}\label{aux}
The helper.
\end{lemma}

\noindent {\it Proof of Theorem~\ref{main}.} By the helper. \qed

\textbf{Proof of Lemma \ref{aux}.} The key step. \qed
\end{document}
